title: Efficient Heuristics Generation for Solving Combinatorial Optimization Problems Using Large Language Models

problem.claim: LLMs are used to autonomously generate heuristics for combinatorial optimization problems by producing search directions and deriving heuristics.

gap.claim: Prompts often lack task-specific knowledge, producing unspecific search directions, while evaluating semantically equivalent heuristics can require unnecessary computing resources.

contributions.claim: Hercules uses Core Abstraction Prompting to abstract core components from elite heuristics and incorporate them as prior knowledge in prompts.

Few-shot Performance Prediction Prompting predicts fitness values for newly derived heuristics from semantic similarity to previously evaluated heuristics, with mechanisms for predictive accuracy and unreliable-prediction detection.
Hercules-P integrates PPP to reduce the computing resources required for evaluating derived heuristics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a theoretical proof concerning CAP's reduction of unspecificity and empirical results.

Experiments across four heuristic-generation tasks, five combinatorial optimization problems, and eight LLMs are reported to show that Hercules outperforms prior LLM-based heuristic-generation algorithms, while Hercules-P minimizes required computing resources.
Ablation studies are reported for CAP, PPP, and the other proposed mechanisms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior work uses LLMs to generate heuristics through search directions and heuristic derivation.
Unspecific prompts and resource-intensive evaluation limit heuristic quality and efficiency.
Hercules introduces CAP, while PPP predicts heuristic fitness and supports unreliable-prediction detection.
Hercules-P applies PPP to improve resource efficiency.
The authors report broad experiments and ablations evaluating the proposed methods.

source_observation.claim: Task-specific knowledge is incorporated into prompts by abstracting core components from elite heuristics.

interpretation.claim: Prompting informed by structured knowledge from strong prior solutions may produce more specific search directions.

application.claim: For LLM-based heuristic generation, consider extracting reusable structural components from high-quality existing heuristics as prompt context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the evaluated heuristic-generation tasks and problems.

source_observation.claim: Fitness prediction uses semantic similarity to previously evaluated heuristics to reduce evaluation resources.

interpretation.claim: Similarity-based surrogate evaluation can prioritize or filter expensive assessments when candidate solutions are semantically related.

application.claim: In expensive heuristic evaluation pipelines, consider predicting candidate performance from comparable evaluated heuristics before allocating full resources.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify prediction error bounds, failure modes, or the conditions under which predictions are unreliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four heuristic-generation tasks or five combinatorial optimization problems.
The abstract does not report quantitative performance or resource-reduction values.
The abstract does not describe the eight LLMs, baselines, or experimental settings.
